questions.prompt: You need a group that will contain Windows devices so an administrator can target them. Which group should you create?
options: A Microsoft 365 group with assigned membership
A Microsoft 365 group with dynamic device membership
A security group
A distribution list
questions.explanation: Security groups can contain users, devices, service principals and other groups. Microsoft 365 groups can contain users only, so they can't hold devices at all.
why_not: Microsoft 365 groups can contain users only; a device can't be a member.
A dynamic device rule still produces device members, and a Microsoft 365 group can't hold devices. Device-based dynamic groups must be security groups.
Distribution lists are managed in Exchange or the Microsoft 365 admin center and don't hold devices for access management.

questions.prompt: A group will be assigned a Microsoft Entra role. The HR team wants its membership to follow the department attribute automatically. What should you tell them?
options: Role-assignable groups require assigned membership, so membership must be managed manually or by another process
Use a dynamic user rule on department
Use a Microsoft 365 group, which supports dynamic rules for role assignment
Nest a dynamic group inside the role-assignable group
questions.explanation: Role-assignable groups require assigned (not dynamic) membership. That prevents anyone who can edit a user attribute from granting themselves a directory role.
why_not: Dynamic membership isn't allowed on role-assignable groups.
The membership rule, not the group type, is the problem: role-assignable groups need assigned membership whatever their type.
Nesting doesn't turn dynamic membership into an allowed path for role assignment, and it adds a second indirection an auditor would reject.

questions.prompt: You created a dynamic group with the rule user.department -eq "Sales". A manager asks you to add a contractor in the Finance department to the group. What should you do?
options: Add the contractor as a member on the group's Members page
Add the contractor as a group owner
Convert the contractor to a guest user
Change the contractor's department, or change the rule so it matches them
questions.explanation: Members of a dynamic group can't be added or removed by hand. Membership comes from the rule, so change the rule or the attribute it reads.
why_not: Manual membership changes are blocked on dynamic groups.
Owners manage a group; they don't become members, and they can't hand-edit a dynamic group's membership either.
User type doesn't affect whether a department rule matches.

questions.prompt: A new user doesn't appear in a dynamic group whose rule is user.department -eq "Sales". Their department reads "Sales " with a trailing space. What is the cause?
options: String comparison in rules is case sensitive
The value doesn't equal "Sales" because of the trailing space; string comparisons aren't case sensitive, but the characters must match
Dynamic groups only evaluate new users once a day
The user needs a licence assigned before rules evaluate
questions.explanation: String and regex operations in membership rules aren't case sensitive, but -eq still compares the whole value, and a trailing space makes it a different string.
why_not: Rule string operations aren't case sensitive; case isn't the problem here.
Rules are re-evaluated when attributes change; the value itself doesn't match.
Dynamic group membership needs the organisation to own enough P1 licences, but they aren't assigned per user, and a licence wouldn't change the string comparison.

questions.sub_skill: Manage licenses in Microsoft Entra ID
questions.prompt: You try to assign a licence to a newly created cloud user and the assignment fails. The tenant has licences available. What should you check first?
options: The user's usage location
Whether the user has MFA registered
Whether the user is in a dynamic group
The user's job title
questions.explanation: A licence can't be assigned to a user whose usage location isn't set, because some services aren't available in every country.
why_not: MFA registration has no bearing on licence assignment.
Dynamic membership doesn't block licence assignment.
Job title is irrelevant to licensing; usage location is the prerequisite.

questions.sub_skill: Manage licenses in Microsoft Entra ID
questions.prompt: Group A is licensed for a product. Group B is a member of Group A. Users who are only in Group B don't have the product. Why?
options: Group B is a Microsoft 365 group
Licences propagate to nested groups only after 24 hours
Group-based licensing doesn't support nested groups; only first-level members of Group A get the licence
Group B needs its own usage location
questions.explanation: Group-based licensing assigns licences to the first-level members of the licensed group only. Assign the licence to Group B too, or add the users to Group A directly.
why_not: The group type of Group B doesn't matter; nesting is the problem.
There's no delayed propagation to nested groups: nested groups are simply not supported for licensing.
Usage location is a user property, and users without one inherit the tenant location under group-based licensing.

questions.prompt: A project manager with no admin role must be able to invite external partners. Invitations are currently limited to users with specific admin roles. What is the least-privileged way to enable this?
options: Assign the User Administrator role
Assign the Guest Inviter role
Assign the Global Administrator role
Change guest invite settings to allow anyone, including guests
questions.explanation: The Guest Inviter role lets a user send invitations even when invitations are restricted to admin roles, without granting a broader administrator role.
why_not: User Administrator can invite, but it also manages every user and group: far more than needed.
Global Administrator is never the least-privileged answer for a single capability.
Opening invitations to everyone, including existing guests, widens access for the whole tenant to solve one person's need.

questions.prompt: Cross-tenant access settings allow B2B collaboration with all Microsoft Entra organisations. The external collaboration settings deny invitations to fabrikam.com. A user tries to invite someone at fabrikam.com. What happens?
options: The invitation succeeds because cross-tenant access settings take precedence
The invitation succeeds but the guest can't sign in
The invitation is sent for admin approval
The invitation is blocked; the most restrictive setting applies
questions.explanation: Cross-tenant access settings and external collaboration settings are evaluated together, and the most restrictive setting applies. The deny list blocks the invitation.
why_not: Neither setting overrides the other: the more restrictive one applies.
The deny list stops the invitation from being sent at all.
There's no built-in approval queue for blocked domain invitations.

questions.prompt: You enable SSPR for a pilot group and test it with your Global Administrator account. It asks for two methods and won't offer security questions, although your user policy requires one method. What explains this?
options: SSPR is misconfigured for the pilot group
Global Administrators can't use SSPR
Administrator accounts use a fixed two-gate policy that requires two methods and prohibits security questions
The tenant needs password writeback
questions.explanation: Accounts holding administrator roles are enabled for SSPR under a strong two-gate policy that you can't change. Test SSPR with a non-administrator account.
why_not: The pilot configuration isn't what the admin account follows.
Administrators are enabled for SSPR by default; they just follow a different policy.
Writeback matters only for users whose passwords are managed on-premises.

questions.prompt: Users synchronised from on-premises Active Directory must be able to reset their passwords through SSPR, and the new password must work on-premises. What is required?
options: Password writeback, with a licence that includes it such as Microsoft Entra ID P1 or Microsoft 365 Business Premium
SSPR enabled for All users is enough
Microsoft Entra ID Free with SSPR enabled
Converting the users to cloud-only accounts first
questions.explanation: When a password is managed on-premises, SSPR works only if writeback is configured, and on-premises writeback requires Entra ID P1/P2 or Microsoft 365 Business Premium.
why_not: Without writeback, users whose passwords are managed on-premises are told to contact an administrator.
Entra ID Free covers only cloud-user password change, not reset or writeback.
Converting accounts isn't needed and would break the on-premises identity the scenario depends on.
